issues.issue: The amount and arithmetic are correct, but Capital appropriations (22.5M) is kept out of receipts. The cash flow statement (p3) shows 'Property taxes - capital improvement fund 20,973,105', which suggests this is mostly a capital property tax levy. Someone should decide whether it is revenue or a capital contribution. The loss on disposal is also netted into the same figure.

Expenses are listed by object, and all three lines are assigned to instruction. The General Fund schedule (p4) shows only about 43% of spending is Instruction; the rest is academic support, student service, institutional administration and physical plant (support services). The function split is a guess; review is already set. This also applies to disbursements[1] and disbursements[2].
Depreciation is put in 'other' while the other object-only lines were given a function (instruction). The treatment is inconsistent; this is a judgment call.
This is the noncurrent compensated absences, but the rules limit 'accrued liabilities' to compensated absences due soon. 'other liabilities' (or long-term) may fit better.

Personnel services probably includes benefits (the notes say so), and all five departmental 'Personnel services' lines are entered as salaries and wages only. The same applies to detail[4], [8], [12] and [16].
